title: Seaport Museum Hosts Free Diwali Celebration in New York on November 10
excerpt: Diya decorating, rangoli, puppet storytime and a dance workshop fill a free two-hour programme at 213 Water Street, presented with The Culture Tree and the Rubin Museum.
body:
• The South Street Seaport Museum hosts a free Diwali celebration on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, from 4:00 to 6:00 p.m. EST at 213 Water Street in New York.
  • The programme is timed: henna from 4:00 to 5:00 p.m., Diwali Puppet Storytime at 4:15 p.m., and an interactive dance workshop at 5:00 p.m., with diya decorating and rangoli making running throughout.
  • Admission is free, according to the museum, and includes access to the museum's Maritime City exhibition; preregistration is encouraged and walkups are accommodated as space allows.
  • The event is presented with The Culture Tree Collective Inc. and the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art.

The South Street Seaport Museum will mark Diwali with a free, family-focused celebration on the museum's Water Street cobblestones, presented in partnership with The Culture Tree Collective Inc. and the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art. The two-hour programme mixes the festival's best-known symbols — rows of lamps, rangoli designs and dance — into timed activities families can join in sequence, and, according to the museum, it doubles as a free entry point to the museum's Maritime City exhibition.

Plan Your Visit

  • Date: Tuesday, November 10, 2026
  • Time: 4:00–6:00 p.m. EST
  • Venue: South Street Seaport Museum
  • Address: 213 Water Street, New York, NY 10038
  • Admission: Free; preregistration is encouraged, walkups accommodated as possible
  • Parking: Not stated in the announcement — check the official event page before you go.
  • Official page: Diwali Celebration at the Seaport Museum

What is on, and when

Throughout the two hours, visitors can decorate a battery-operated, diya-inspired candle and float it in a special pool, a gesture the museum describes as symbolizing prosperity for the new year — Diwali, it notes, also marks the start of the Hindu New Year. Rubin Teaching Artists will guide families in creating a large-scale rangoli design with flower petals, and attendees can make their own smaller rangoli designs using sand. A henna artist is available from 4:00 to 5:00 p.m.

At 4:15 p.m. the programme moves into the museum's first-floor Maritime City exhibition gallery for Diwali Puppet Storytime, covering the significance and origins of Diwali and how it is celebrated worldwide, including a reading of A Kids Book About Diwali. At 5:00 p.m. an interactive dance workshop and performance follows, built around popular Diwali songs, music and stories; attendees learn mudras, the hand gestures used in classical dance forms. The Rubin Museum lists the dance workshop as running from 5:00 to 5:30 p.m.

What else the visit includes

Admission to the event includes free access to the Maritime City exhibition, which traces how New York grew from its origins as a seaport, and to Bowne & Co., Stationers, the museum's 19th-century-style print shop, where visitors can print a keepsake on the museum's historic press. The museum notes that access to Bowne & Co. involves walking up and down a few stairs, and that access to its additional exhibitions and historic ships is not included with the event ticket.

The partners

The Culture Tree Collective Inc. promotes cultural literacy about South Asia through language, educational and cultural programmes, with a stated goal of building empathy and understanding across cultures. The Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art, founded in 2004, now operates without a centralized physical space and runs programmes globally. Its own event page recommends pre-registration and lists the same timed programme. Families planning to attend can register through the Seaport Museum's event page; the museum says walkups will be accommodated as possible.
